On lapse: A pending swap lapses at the earlier of 48 hours after it was requested and the start of the shift. From that moment (inclusive) it is `expired`, whatever operation looks at it, and it can no longer be accepted, declined or cancelled (a Conflict on param `swap`). On rest: When accepting, the person taking the shift must have at least 10 hours between this shift and each of their other shifts (end of one to start of the next; exactly 10 hours is fine, an overlap counts as less). Shift swaps for rota: a few product decisions are open. My default for each is in brackets; tell me if you want something different.

1. Expiry: the status list includes `expired`, but the request doesn't say when a swap expires. What triggers it? [Default: a swap still `pending` when its shift's start time has passed becomes `expired`. It can no longer be accepted, declined or cancelled, and it is marked expired the next time any swap operation runs.]

2. Several swaps for one shift: can a shift have more than one pending swap at once? [Default: no. Requesting a swap for a shift that already has a pending swap raises Conflict on `shift`.]

3. Who may act on a swap? The API has no caller identity, so nothing stops anyone calling any operation. [Default: no caller checks. The rule is only that the swap must be `pending` for accept/decline/cancel. Recording who acted is left for later.]

4. Accepting when the receiver is busy: if `to_staff` already has a shift that overlaps, should accept fail? [Default: yes. Accept raises Conflict on `swap`, using the same overlap rule as shift.create, and the swap stays pending.]

5. Offering to someone who is not staff: [Default: NotFound on `to_staff`, the same as shift.create.]

6. Does a shift that is part of a pending swap stay editable or deletable? There is no shift update or delete operation today, so this only matters later. [Default: no action needed now.]
